author: sonnet
label: climb-04-01
changes: Added an opening summary and a description of the existing system (two instances, load balancer, users table, sign-up out of scope), because newcomers could not tell where users or instances came from.
Added a short Terms list (session, idle and absolute limits, throttle).
Added a Throttle scope row to the decisions table stating the lock is by email only, not IP.
Added a Login page rule: GET /login shows the form, knows nothing of lockout, and does not redirect signed-in users.
Added the lock wait behaviour: a second attempt waits on the row lock with a 5-second lock_timeout, then fails as a 503.
Said that one shared middleware runs the session check on all non-login routes and attaches user_id as the current user.
Said the cleanup sweep runs from an in-process timer, retries on the next tick after a failure, and what happens when it meets a locked throttle row.
Reordered into the newcomer layout: summary and how the app works today, terms, decisions, state, diagram, numbered steps, failure table, open questions.

Merged the separate Login page, Login attempt, Session creation, Protected request check, Logout, Cleanup and Storage failure sections into four numbered steps, each with trigger, action, data and failure handling.
Merged the storage-failure rules into the steps and one failure table, replacing the separate storage failure section.
Merged the Session storage and Failure counts decision rows into one row, and removed the Why column repetition for throttle and fixation notes.
Cut the Requirement coverage table, which repeated the steps and used numeric codes pointing elsewhere.
Cut the duplicate wording of the 401/429 rules between the rules text and the diagram notes, and removed the section-number references.
Moved login CSRF and the bcrypt-held row lock into a short Open questions section at the end.
Left the sequence diagram, SQL and all design decisions unchanged.
